7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.2: CPU time spent executing work on the selected node, excluding idle, I/O wait and stolen time. Each stacked core contributes its share of total node CPU capacity; a full stack at 100% means all logical CPUs are busy. Rates use Grafana’s sampling window.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.3: System load averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, with the logical CPU count as a reference. Load is a count of tasks, not CPU usage in percent. On Linux it includes runnable tasks and tasks in uninterruptible sleep, often waiting for I/O; a sustained load above the CPU count can indicate contention.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.8: Per-device read and write throughput in bytes per second, plus the percentage of time the device had I/O in progress. Busy time is not a measure of free disk space or maximum throughput. Only devices matching the dashboard’s disk-name filter are included; an unsupported name or missing exporter counter produces no series.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.9: Filesystem capacity, available space and derived used space for each mount point on the selected node. Used space is capacity minus space available to ordinary processes, so reserved blocks also count as unavailable. Sizes are shown in bytes and usage as a percentage; a value near 100% means little writable space remains.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.11: Incoming network traffic for each exported interface except the interface named lo, in bits per second. This is traffic volume per second, not a percentage of link capacity. Virtual interfaces can carry the same traffic as a physical interface, so their values should not be added blindly.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.12: Outgoing network traffic for each exported interface except the interface named lo, in bits per second. This is traffic volume per second, not a percentage of link capacity. A missing interface series means no matching counter was collected, not necessarily zero traffic.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.5: Physical RAM split into used memory, buffers, file cache and free memory, in bytes. Used memory here is total minus free, buffers and cached memory. Cache is useful and may be reclaimed; this breakdown therefore differs from the adjacent usage gauge, which uses the kernel’s available-memory estimate.
7d57716318ee0dddbac5a7f451fb7753.6: Percentage of physical RAM that is not available for new work: 100 × (1 − MemAvailable / MemTotal). MemAvailable includes memory the kernel expects to reclaim, making this more useful than free RAM alone. Sustained high usage suggests memory pressure; it does not by itself prove an out-of-memory condition.

7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.2: CPU time spent executing work on the selected node, excluding idle, I/O wait and stolen time. Each stacked core contributes its share of total node CPU capacity; a full stack at 100% means all logical CPUs are busy. Rates use Grafana’s sampling window.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.3: System load averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, with the exported logical CPU count as a reference. Load is the operating system’s task-demand estimate, not CPU usage in percent. Compare sustained load with CPU capacity and other resource metrics before concluding the node is overloaded.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.8: Per-device read and write throughput in bytes per second, plus the percentage of time the device had I/O in progress. Busy time is not a measure of free disk space or maximum throughput. Only devices matching the dashboard’s disk-name filter are included; an unsupported name or missing exporter counter produces no series.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.9: Filesystem capacity, available space and derived used space for each mount point on the selected node. Used space is capacity minus space available to ordinary processes, so reserved blocks also count as unavailable. Sizes are shown in bytes and usage as a percentage; a value near 100% means little writable space remains.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.11: Incoming network traffic for each exported interface except the interface named lo, in bits per second. This is traffic volume per second, not a percentage of link capacity. Virtual interfaces can carry the same traffic as a physical interface, so their values should not be added blindly.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.12: Outgoing network traffic for each exported interface except the interface named lo, in bits per second. This is traffic volume per second, not a percentage of link capacity. A missing interface series means no matching counter was collected, not necessarily zero traffic.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.5: Total physical RAM and RAM in use on the selected AIX node, in bytes. Used memory is calculated as total minus available memory. This panel requires AIX memory counters; selecting a Linux node can leave it empty even when Linux monitoring is healthy.
7e0a61e486f727d763fb1d86fdd629c2.6: Percentage of RAM in use on the selected AIX node, calculated as 100 × (1 − available / total). Higher values leave less memory available to new work. The AIX-specific counters are absent on Linux nodes, so an empty panel there is expected.

629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.2: CPU time spent executing work on the selected node, excluding idle, I/O wait and stolen time. Each stacked core contributes its share of total node CPU capacity; a full stack at 100% means all logical CPUs are busy. Rates use Grafana’s sampling window.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.3: System load averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes, with the exported logical CPU count as a reference. Load is the operating system’s task-demand estimate, not CPU usage in percent. Compare sustained load with CPU capacity and other resource metrics before concluding the node is overloaded.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.8: Per-device read and write throughput in bytes per second, plus the percentage of time the device had I/O in progress. Busy time is not a measure of free disk space or maximum throughput. Only devices matching the dashboard’s disk-name filter are included; an unsupported name or missing exporter counter produces no series.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.9: Filesystem capacity, available space and derived used space for each mount point on the selected node. Used space is capacity minus space available to ordinary processes, so reserved blocks also count as unavailable. Sizes are shown in bytes and usage as a percentage; a value near 100% means little writable space remains.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.11: Incoming network traffic for each exported interface except the interface named lo, in bits per second. This is traffic volume per second, not a percentage of link capacity. Virtual interfaces can carry the same traffic as a physical interface, so their values should not be added blindly.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.12: Outgoing network traffic for each exported interface except the interface named lo, in bits per second. This is traffic volume per second, not a percentage of link capacity. A missing interface series means no matching counter was collected, not necessarily zero traffic.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.5: Physical RAM on the selected macOS node, in bytes: total capacity, application memory (internal minus purgeable), wired memory and compressed memory. The used-memory line is the sum of those three components; do not add it to its components again. These macOS counters are not exported by Linux nodes.
629701ea43bf69291922ea45f4a87d37.6: RAM usage on the selected macOS node as a percentage of total physical RAM. Used memory is internal minus purgeable, plus wired and compressed memory. This panel requires macOS-specific counters; an empty result on a Linux node does not indicate a monitoring outage.

fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.2: Share of the selected node’s CPU capacity spent doing work, averaged over five minutes and shown as a percentage. Sustained values near 100% mean little idle CPU capacity remains; this does not measure the number of tasks waiting for CPU. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.3: One-minute Linux load average divided by the selected node’s logical CPU count. A ratio of 1 (displayed as 100%) means one runnable or uninterruptible task per CPU on average. This is a pressure indicator, not CPU utilization; disk waits can raise it even when CPU usage is low. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.5: Share of the selected node’s physical RAM that is not available for new work, shown as a percentage. The available-memory estimate accounts for reclaimable memory. High usage should be interpreted together with major page faults and application failures. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.6: Major page faults per second on the selected node, averaged over five minutes. These occur when a requested memory page must be read from storage; they may come from file reads or swapping and are not automatically errors. Sustained increases alongside high RAM usage can indicate memory pressure. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.8: Incoming and outgoing throughput on physical network interfaces of the selected node, averaged over five minutes, in bytes per second. Transmit traffic is drawn below zero to separate directions; it is not a negative byte count. This is not a percentage of network capacity. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.9: Packets dropped on receive or transmit on the selected node’s physical interfaces, per second over five minutes. Drops can indicate queue pressure or networking problems; correlate them with traffic and application errors. Transmit values are drawn below zero only to separate directions. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.11: Fraction of time each disk on the selected node had I/O in progress, averaged over five minutes and displayed as a percentage. Values near 100% indicate a continuously busy device, but parallel SSDs can still have spare throughput. This does not measure disk space. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.12: Average number of I/O operations in progress or queued for each disk on the selected node, derived from weighted I/O time over five minutes. A value of 1 means one operation outstanding on average. Sustained growth can indicate storage contention; the useful threshold depends on device parallelism. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
fac67cfbe174d3ef53eb473d73d9212f.14: Filesystem space unavailable to ordinary processes on the selected node, as a percentage of capacity for each device. Calculated as 1 − available / size, so reserved space is included. Values near 100% mean little writable space remains; this is capacity usage, not disk I/O activity. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.

3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.2: CPU utilization across the selected cluster, averaged over five minutes. Each stacked node contributes busy CPU capacity divided by the cluster’s total logical CPU count; the stack is weighted by node CPU capacity. A total near 100% indicates little idle CPU capacity cluster-wide. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.3: Average one-minute load per logical CPU across the selected cluster, with equal weight for each node. Each stack segment contributes that node’s normalized load divided by the number of nodes. A total ratio of 1 (displayed as 100%) means one runnable or uninterruptible task per CPU on average; this is not CPU usage. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.5: Mean memory utilization across the selected cluster, giving each node equal weight regardless of RAM size. Each stack segment contributes its node’s unavailable-memory fraction divided by the number of nodes. This is not total used bytes divided by total cluster RAM. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.6: Major page faults per second across the selected cluster, averaged over five minutes and stacked by node. A major fault requires reading a memory page from storage; it can reflect file reads or swapping. A sustained increase together with high RAM usage may indicate memory pressure.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.8: Incoming and outgoing traffic across exported non-loopback interfaces, averaged over five minutes, in bytes per second. The stack combines nodes; transmit values are drawn below zero to separate directions. Virtual interfaces can double-count the same traffic, so this is not necessarily the cluster’s external traffic volume. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.9: Receive and transmit packet drops on exported non-loopback interfaces across the selected cluster, per second over five minutes. Transmit values are drawn below zero only to separate directions. Sustained drops can indicate network pressure, but virtual interfaces may report the same traffic at multiple layers. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.11: Mean disk busy-time fraction across all matched node/device series, averaged over five minutes and shown as a percentage. Each stacked device contributes its busy-time fraction divided by the number of devices. A busy individual disk can be hidden by a low cluster average; use the node view to locate it.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.12: Mean number of outstanding I/O operations across all matched node/device series, derived from weighted I/O time over five minutes. Each stacked device contributes its average outstanding operations divided by the number of devices. A total of 1 means one outstanding operation per device on average; inspect individual disks before diagnosing a bottleneck.
3e97d1d02672cdd0861f4c97c64f89b2.14: Filesystem space unavailable to ordinary processes across the selected cluster as a share of total filesystem capacity. Each stacked node contributes its unavailable bytes divided by total capacity, so larger disks have more weight. Reserved space is included; this measures storage capacity, not I/O activity. Exact zero values are filtered by this query, so an idle resource can appear as a gap rather than a line at zero.
